Thanks — here’s a 2-week, hotel-room–friendly maintenance (hold muscle) program you can give your client. It assumes only a yoga mat and a door pull-up bar are available, she’s intermediate and six weeks into a hypertrophy block, and the goal is to maintain strength/muscle, not gain. The plan focuses on maintaining stimulus with moderate volume, preserving movement variety, limited progressive overload (since equipment is minimal), and maintaining nutrition and recovery.

Overview and principles
- Frequency: 4 resistance-focused sessions per week (upper/lower split with one full-body/conditioning day and one active recovery/mobility day). Two rest days.
- Intensity: Moderate (RPE ~6–8). Reps in hypertrophy-ish ranges (8–20) but keep overall volume slightly reduced vs. usual block to avoid trying to make gains.
- Volume: Maintain weekly effective sets for each muscle group (roughly 6–10 work sets/week for major muscle groups) but distribute across bodyweight variations.
- Progressive overload: Use tempo changes, pausing, more reps, unilateral work, or increasing time-under-tension. If possible, use a backpack with clothes as light weight for added resistance on selected movements.
- Conditioning: Short, high-effort metabolic circuits once per week to maintain work capacity.
- Mobility/recovery: Daily mobility short sessions; one active recovery day with longer mobility and optional light steady-state cardio (walking).
- Nutrition: Maintain current caloric intake to hold weight (no surplus). Prioritize protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (aim for ~25–35 g protein per meal), adequate carbs for training days, and hydration. Slightly increase daily protein on heavier sessions if appetite allows. Maintain sleep ~7–9 hours; manage travel stress with routine and light breathing/meditation.
- Equipment substitutions: Door pull-up bar, mat, bodyweight, towel, and a backpack for light loading. If no pull-ups or limited range, use negatives, assisted reps, or horizontal rowing (inverted rows using bar if safe).

Two-week schedule (repeat week 1 pattern for week 2 with small progressions: +1–2 reps per set or slower eccentrics when sessions feel easy)

Weekly layout
- Day 1: Upper push/pull (strength-ish maintenance)
- Day 2: Lower (mainly unilateral/hamstring emphasis)
- Day 3: Rest/active mobility
- Day 4: Upper (hypertrophy emphasis + vertical focus)
- Day 5: Full-body metabolic / conditioning + core
- Day 6: Rest or light walk + mobility
- Day 7: Optional mobility or easy bodyline/core; treat as rest if tired

Guidelines for sets/reps and tempos
- Use controlled 2–4 sec eccentrics for most movements to increase tension without external load. Pause 1–2 seconds at the bottom on some sets to remove momentum.
- For strength maintenance sets keep RPE ~7–8 (2–3 reps left in tank). For hypertrophy sets aim RPE ~7–9 depending on how she feels.
- If a movement becomes easy, increase reps by 1–3 or slow tempo (e.g., 3–4 s eccentric) or add isometric holds or a weighted backpack.

Week 1

Day 1 — Upper (Horizontal Pull/Push focus)
Warm-up: 5–8 min joint mobility + scapular activation (band if available; otherwise wall slides, Y-T-Ws, shoulder circles)

1) Push-ups — 4 sets x 8–15 reps
- Variation: standard or incline/decline using bed edge. Tempo 3s down, 1s pause, explosive up. If <8 reps per set, use knees or perform negatives with slow eccentrics to accumulate TUT.

2) Inverted rows on door/bar or towel row (under door secure or use bar) — 4 sets x 8–12 reps
- Feet bent to adjust difficulty. 3s eccentric.

3) Bulgarian split squat to chest-height support (single-leg pressing motion) — 3 sets x 8–12 each leg
- Use doorframe support for balance; keep chest-up. Can perform rear foot elevated on bed/couch. Adds lower-body and core stability while working upper chain indirectly.

4) Pike push-ups (progress toward vertical pressing) — 3 sets x 6–12 reps
- If too easy, elevate feet to increase load; if too hard, do pike with knees slightly bent or partial ROM negatives. 2–3s eccentric.

5) Doorframe face pulls (hand towel/strap looped over top of closed door) or bandless face pulls (pulling elbows high with external rotation) — 3 sets x 12–15
- Emphasize scapular retraction and external rotation.

Core finisher:
- Dead bug or hollow hold progression — 3 x 30–45 s total work (e.g., 4–6x20–30 s holds with 15–30 s rest)

Cooldown: 5 min thoracic mobility and pec stretch.

Day 2 — Lower (Unilateral + posterior chain emphasis)
Warm-up: 5–8 min hip swings, bodyweight squats, bandless glute bridges

1) Single-leg Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 4 sets x 8–12 each leg
- Slow 3–4 s eccentric, reach toward floor or use a backpack in opposite hand for slight loading.

2) Bulgarian split squat — 4 sets x 8–12 each leg
- Controlled tempo, add backpack if needed.

3) Glute bridge / single-leg glute bridge — 3 sets x 12–20
- Hold top 1–2 s, slow eccentrics. If strong, perform single-leg variations: 3–5 sets x 8–12.

4) Hamstring curl substitute (Nordic style negatives or slider towel curls on mat) — 3 sets x 6–12
- If partner not available for Nordic, perform slider heels curl: heels on towel on floor, slide heels in/out; or single-leg slow bridges to emphasize hamstrings.

5) Calf raises (double or single-leg on step or edge of bed) — 3 sets x 15–25
- Slow eccentric, pause at bottom 1s, full contraction on top.

Core:
- Side plank — 3 x 30–45 s each side
- Bird-dog — 2 sets x 8–10 each side slow control

Cooldown: 5–8 min hamstring and hip flexor stretches, foam roll substitute (tennis ball for glutes).

Day 3 — Active recovery / mobility
- 25–35 min walk, focus on breathing and posture OR 20–30 min yoga flow using mat.
- Mobility sequence: 10–15 min focused on thoracic rotation, hip mobility, shoulder mobility.
- Optional: gentle bandless shoulder work (wall slides, band pull-aparts if travel band available).

Day 4 — Upper (Vertical emphasis + accessory)
Warm-up: 5–8 min joint mobility + scapular pull-ups (scapular shrugs on bar)

1) Pull-ups / Assisted pull-ups / Negative pull-ups — 4 sets x 4–8 (or 6–12 assisted)
- If unable for many reps, do slow 4–6s negatives or band-assisted repetitions. If too easy, add isometric holds at top for 10–20 s.

2) Archer push-ups / wide push-ups / decline push-ups — 4 sets x 6–12
- Choose variation to keep RPE ~7–8.

3) Bent-over single-arm row with backpack — 3 sets x 8–12 each arm
- Controlled 3s eccentric.

4) Doorframe Y-raise or prone T on bed/couch for rear delts — 3 sets x 12–15

5) Triceps dips off bed/chair (if safe) or close-grip push-up — 3 sets x 8–15

Core finisher:
- Hanging knee raises on pull-up bar (if safe) or lying leg raises — 3 sets x 10–15
Cooldown: pec stretch, lats stretch, shoulder mobility.

Day 5 — Full-body metabolic + core
Warm-up: 5 min dynamic movement (bodyweight squats, lunges, arm swings)

Circuit (3–5 rounds; 40s work/20s rest or 45s/15s depending fitness). Keep intensity moderate-high but not maximal. Rest 90–120s between rounds.
- A1) Jump squats or squat pulses (bodyweight) — 40s
- A2) Push-up or incline push-up — 40s
- A3) Reverse lunge alternating — 40s
- A4) Inverted row or horizontal row — 40s
- A5) Mountain climbers or plank shoulder taps — 40s

If impact is an issue, replace jump squats with fast bodyweight squats.

Core:
- Plank ladder: 45s, 30s, 15s (or 3 x 45s) focusing on bracing.

Cooldown: 5–8 min stretching and breathing.

Day 6 — Rest or light active recovery
- 20–40 min easy walk or swim if available. Mobility and foam roll substitute.

Day 7 — Optional mobility / light session or rest
- Short yoga flow (20–30 min), breathing, and foam rolling. If feeling good, do a light skill session: slow pistols to box, ring work, or mobility holds.

Week 2
Repeat week 1 structure with one of these small progressions:
- Add 1–3 reps per set on easier movements OR
- Increase time-under-tension by 1–2 seconds on eccentrics OR
- Add a light backpack (2–8 kg of clothes) for 1–2 compound lifts (split squats, single-arm rows, glute bridges).
- On pull-ups, try to increase total quality reps across the session (e.g., 1 extra rep per set or 1 extra set) or add a 5–10s isometric top hold once per set.
- On conditioning day, add one extra round or reduce rest by 5–10s.

Example adjustments for week 2:
- Day 1: Push-ups sets increase to 4 x 10–15 (if week 1 was 8–12). Inverted rows 4 x 10–14.
- Day 2: Single-leg RDL 4 x 10–12, Bulgarian split squat 4 x 10–12.
- Day 4: Pull-ups aim for 4–5 sets with 1–2 more reps total; add a 10s top hold on last set.

Nutrition specifics for maintenance while traveling
- Calories: Aim for maintenance calories — keep roughly the same as pre-travel. If unsure, track intake for first few days to estimate maintenance and adjust +/- 100–200 kcal if weight trends are off.
- Protein: Aim for 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight/day. For a 32-year-old female of average build, target ~90–120 g/day depending on size — but calculate based on actual weight. Spread protein across meals (~25–40 g per meal).
- Carbs: Maintain moderate carbs around training to support performance (pre/post snack like fruit + yogurt). Don’t drastically cut carbs — they’ll help maintain workout intensity.
- Fats: Keep dietary fats ~20–30% of calories.
- Hydration: Drink water consistently; travel often increases dehydration.
- Alcohol & sodium: Minimize excess alcohol and very salty foods that can alter weight and recovery.

Recovery and sleep
- Prioritize 7–9 hours sleep; use sleep hygiene strategies (dark room, consistent routine).
- Use breathing/relaxation or short bedtime mobility routines to sleep on travel nights.
- If sleep is disrupted, reduce session intensity next day and emphasize mobility.

Coaching cues and monitoring
- Ask client to rate session RPE and note soreness daily. If RPE consistently >8 or recovery poor, reduce volume by 20–30%.
- Track bodyweight once mid-travel and again at end; small fluctuations due to hydration are normal. Adjust food if client gains >1–1.5 kg and wants strict maintenance.
- Encourage protein-rich snacks (Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, protein bars if available) to hit targets.

Minimal equipment quick options
- Backpack: fill with clothes/ books to add 2–10 kg.
- Towel: for rows and sliding hamstring curls.
- Chair/bed edge: for dips, elevated split squats, foot support.

Return-to-gym transition

- Frequency: 4 resistance sessions/week + 1 full‑body metabolic session + 2 easy recovery days.
- Session length: resistance ~30–45 min + 15‑minute finisher.
- Tempo: use slow eccentrics (3–4 s), 0–2 s pause, controlled concentric. For negatives use 4–6 s descents.
- Target RPE: 6–8. Leave 1–3 reps in reserve for most sets; one set per exercise can be a bit closer to failure.
- Nutrition: maintain calories; protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; hydrate; sleep 7–9 h.
- Tracking: use Session Quality (SQ) 1–10 after each resistance session; weekly SQ average target ~6–8. Also track one weekly objective rep total (e.g., total pull‑ups and push‑ups) and one weekly morning bodyweight.

Weekly layout (same each week)
- Day 1: Upper (horizontal push/pull)
- Day 2: Lower (unilateral + posterior)
- Day 3: Active recovery / mobility
- Day 4: Upper (vertical) — Week 1 has active‑rest option if tired
- Day 5: Full‑body metabolic + core
- Day 6: Rest or light active recovery
- Day 7: Optional mobility / light session or rest

Week 1 — Moderate maintenance (with active‑rest option on Day 4)

Day 1 — Upper (Horizontal emphasis)
Warm‑up (5–8 min)
- Shoulder circles, scapular shrugs on bar, thoracic rotations, cat–cow.

Resistance
1) Push‑ups — 4 sets x 8–15 reps (3s down, 1s pause)
- Adjust incline/decline to set RPE ~6–8.

2) Inverted rows (door pull‑up bar or towel row if needed) — 4 sets x 8–12 reps (3s eccentric)
- Adjust foot position for difficulty.

3) Incline single‑arm push‑up progression or narrow push‑ups — 3 sets x 6–10 each side (or 8–12 symmetric)
- Control tempo.

4) Doorframe face pulls / bandless rear delt pulls — 3 sets x 12–15 reps

Core finisher
- Hollow hold or dead‑bug — 3 rounds totaling 20–40 s work (e.g., 4 × 20–30 s holds with short rests).

15‑minute Cardio finisher (choose format)
- EMOM: alternate Minute A: 40s mountain climbers; Minute B: 12 burpees — repeat ~7–8 cycles.
- AMRAP: 15 min — 10 burpees, 40 mountain climbers (count both legs), 15 fast squats.
- Intervals: 30s on / 30s off of squat jumps (or fast air squats) and plank jacks / mountain climbers.

Cooldown (3–5 min)
- Shoulder/pec stretch, breathing.

Day 2 — Lower (Unilateral + posterior)
Warm‑up (5–8 min)
- Leg swings, glute bridges, air squats.

Resistance
1) Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight) — 4 sets x 8–12 each leg (3–4s eccentric)

2) Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on bed/chair) — 4 sets x 8–12 each leg (2–3s eccentric)

3) Glute bridge → single‑leg glute bridge — 3 sets x 12–20 (or 3–5 sets x 8–12 single‑leg as able); 1s top pause.

4) Hamstring slide (towel sliders) or Nordic‑style negatives — 3 sets x 6–12 reps

5) Calf raises — 3 sets x 15–25 reps (slow eccentrics)

Core
- Side plank — 3 x 30–45 s each side
- Bird‑dog — 2 x 8–10 each side

15‑minute Cardio finisher (choose format)
- EMOM: Minute 1 — 40s fast alternating reverse lunges; Minute 2 — 12 jump lunges (or 20 step‑through lunges) — repeat.
- AMRAP: 15 min — 20 walking lunges, 15 tuck/squat jumps (or squat pulses), 10 burpees (or incline burpees).
- Intervals: 40s on / 20s off of alternating jump lunges and high knees.

Cooldown (3–5 min)
- Hamstring and hip flexor stretches.

Day 3 — Active recovery / mobility
- 20–35 min brisk walk OR 20–30 min yoga flow.
- Mobility circuit 10–15 min: thoracic rotations, 90/90 hip switches, wall slides, gentle couch stretch.

Optional light 15‑minute finisher (very low intensity)
- 15 min brisk walking or easy stair climb (RPE 3–4).

Day 4 — Upper (Vertical emphasis) — Active‑rest option if tired
Standard session (if not tired)
Warm‑up (5–8 min)
- Scapular shrugs on bar, arm circles.

Resistance
1) Pull‑ups / assisted pull‑ups / negatives — 4 sets x 3–8 reps (or assisted 6–12)
- If limited, do slow negatives (4–6s) or top holds.

2) Pike push‑ups — 4 sets x 6–12 reps (elevate feet for more difficulty)

3) Inverted row (different grip) or archer row variation — 3 sets x 8–12

4) Doorframe Y‑raises / prone T‑raises — 3 sets x 12–15

5) Triceps dips off bed/chair or diamond push‑ups — 3 sets x 8–15

Core finisher
- Hanging knee raises (if bar allows) or lying leg raises — 3 sets x 10–15

15‑minute Cardio finisher (choose format)
- EMOM: alternate 12 burpees and 40s mountain climbers; or AMRAP of burpees, plank taps, fast squats; or intervals 30/30.

Cooldown (3–5 min)
- Lats/pec stretch, breathing.

Active‑rest option (if she’s tired) — low effort session (25–35 min total, RPE 3–5)
If she chooses active rest instead of the standard Day 4 session, use the following low‑intensity, movement‑focused plan:

1) Gentle mobilization / joint prep — 6–8 min
- 2 min marching in place; shoulder mobility flow; thoracic rotations; cat–cow transitions.

2) Low‑load movement & mobility circuit — 12–15 min (2–3 rounds, 60–90s rest)
- Slow bodyweight squats → deep squat hold (8–10 reps, last rep hold 10–15s)
- Incline or wall push‑ups (8–10 slow reps)
- Glute bridges (10–12 controlled reps)
- Scapular pull‑ups / scapular shrugs on bar (6–8 reps)
- Dead‑bug or bird‑dog (6–8 each side)

3) Short breathing + mobility finish — 6–8 min
- Pectoral/lat stretch, hip flexor stretch, 2–3 min guided breathing.

Optional light 10‑minute finisher only if energy permits (very low intensity)
- 10 min steady marching in place or brisk walk (RPE 3–4). Skip if fatigue significant.

Note: Mark this as Active‑Rest session in tracking (SQ ~4–6). Recovery is the goal.

Day 5 — Full‑body metabolic + core
Warm‑up (5 min)
- Dynamic mobility.

Circuit — 3 rounds (work 40s / rest 20s) or 4 rounds if she feels good
- Bodyweight squats
- Push‑ups
- Alternating reverse lunges
- Inverted rows
- Plank shoulder taps / mountain climbers

Core
- Plank ladder: 45s, 30s, 15s (or 3 × 45s)

15‑minute Cardio finisher (choose format)
- AMRAP 15: 10 burpees, 20 mountain climbers (per leg = 40), 30 fast squats.
- Or Intervals: 40s on / 20s off alternating squat jumps and mountain climbers.

Cooldown (3–5 min)
- Full‑body stretch and breathing.

Day 6 — Rest or light active recovery
- 20–40 min easy walk, mobility, tennis ball glute release.
- Optional very light 15‑minute finish (15 min brisk walk) if desired — keep RPE 2–4.

Day 7 — Optional mobility / light session or rest
- 20–30 min yoga flow and mobility. If energy is high, do a light skills/strength session (e.g., pistol progressions or pull‑up practice) but keep volume low.

Week 2 — Slightly harder (feel like progress while staying sensible)
Key changes vs Week 1:
- Slightly harder variations, small volume increases (+1 set on 1–2 compounds or +2–4 reps per set), one controlled overload technique per major lift (slow negatives, longer isometrics, pauses).
- Cardio finishers are a bit tougher (extra rounds, shorter rest, higher pace).
- Monitor fatigue closely and scale back if SQ drops or sleep is poor.

Day 1 — Upper (Horizontal) — harder
Warm‑up (5–8 min)

Resistance (adjustments)
1) Push‑ups — 4 sets x 10–18 reps (add 2–3 reps per set or switch 1–2 sets to decline/single‑arm progressions)
- One set: 2s pause at bottom.

2) Inverted rows — 4–5 sets x 8–14 reps
- Last set: 4–5s eccentric negatives.

3) Incline single‑arm push‑up progression / archer push‑ups — 3–4 sets x 6–10 each side (or equivalent)
- Add 1 set if energy allows.

4) Doorframe face pulls / rear delt pulls — 3–4 sets x 12–15

Core
- Hollow hold / dead‑bug — 3 rounds, increase hold times by 5–10s.

15‑minute Cardio finisher — push a bit harder
- AMRAP 15: 10 burpees, 60 mountain climbers (per leg = 120 total counted as 60/side if counting both legs), 20 fast squats — push pace but maintain form.
- Or EMOM: Minute 1 — 45s mountain climbers; Minute 2 — 12 burpees; repeat.

Cooldown

Day 2 — Lower (harder)
Warm‑up (5–8 min)

Resistance (adjustments)
1) Single‑leg RDL — 4 sets x 10–14 each leg (add 2 reps)
- Final set: 3s pause at bottom for 1–2 reps.

2) Bulgarian split squat — 4–5 sets x 8–14 each leg (add set or reps)
- Last set: 5s isometric bottom hold on 1–2 reps.

3) Glute bridge / single‑leg bridge — 4 sets x 10–15 (more single‑leg work)

4) Hamstring slides / Nordic negatives — 3–4 sets x 6–12 (slow eccentrics)

5) Calf raises — 3–4 sets x 15–30 (add pause at bottom on last set)

Core
- Side plank +10–15s; bird‑dog slow 2–3 sets.

15‑minute Cardio finisher — harder
- Intervals 40s on / 20s off: jump lunges (or fast alternating reverse lunges) and high knees.
- Or AMRAP 15: 20 walking lunges, 15 squat jumps, 10 burpees.

Cooldown

Day 3 — Active recovery / mobility (slightly more purposeful)
- Mobility flow plus a 10‑minute easy movement block (brisk walk, easy stair climb, or continuous low‑effort bodyweight movement at RPE 4).

Day 4 — Upper (Vertical) — harder but watch fatigue
Warm‑up (5–8 min)

Resistance (adjustments)
1) Pull‑ups / assisted / negatives — 4–5 sets x 4–8 reps (add 1 rep per set or extra set)
- Add one set of slow negatives or a 5–8s top isometric on last set.

2) Pike push‑ups — 4 sets x 8–14 reps (elevate feet if able)
- One set: 2–3s pause at bottom / partial rep isometric.

3) Inverted row / archer row — 3–4 sets x 8–12

4) Doorframe Y/T raises — 3–4 sets x 12–15

5) Triceps dips / diamond push‑ups — 3–4 sets x 8–15

Core
- Hanging knee raises / lying leg raises — 3–4 sets x 12–18

15‑minute Cardio finisher — harder
- EMOM: Minute 1 — 12 burpees; Minute 2 — 45s mountain climbers; repeat for 15 min.
- If very fatigued, substitute with lower impact AMRAP or intervals.

Cooldown

Day 5 — Full‑body metabolic + core — higher intensity
Warm‑up (5 min)

Circuit adjustments
- Increase to 4 rounds or extend work interval (e.g., 45s/15s).
- Push tempo for slightly higher reps per interval.

Core
- 3–4 x 45–60s planks.

15‑minute Cardio finisher — push for a new benchmark
- AMRAP 15: 10 burpees, 20 mountain climbers (per leg), 30 fast squats — aim to exceed Week 1 totals.
- Or intervals 30s on / 30s off high intensity (burpee alternative / squat jumps) and mountain climbers.

Cooldown

Day 6 — Rest or light active recovery
- 20–40 min easy walk; mobility. Short nap if needed. Skip extra conditioning unless fully recovered.

Day 7 — Optional mobility / low‑volume progress session
Voluntary “feel‑good” progress options (pick one)
- Pull‑up practice: 6–8 sets of 3–5 challenging reps/negatives with long rest (focus on quality).
- Or Single‑leg strength: 6 sets of single‑leg RDLs to depth, slow eccentrics.
- Or keep it as a mobility/yoga session. This day is optional — listen to fatigue.

Recovery & nutrition reminders
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day. Aim for 20–40 g protein per meal/snack.
- Calories: aim for maintenance. If uncertain, keep pre‑travel intake; adjust ±100–200 kcal if bodyweight trend shows >1 kg change.
- Hydration: sip water frequently; increase on flight days.
- Sleep: prioritize 7–9 hours; use blackout, routine, breathing tools.
- If sleep or SQ falls: reduce volume/finishers and emphasize mobility and sleep.

Daily & weekly tracking (simple)
- After each resistance session record Session Quality (SQ) 1–10 and note one‑line sleep/soreness.
- Track weekly sum of key reps (example: pull‑ups total & push‑ups total) and one weekly morning bodyweight (same time day).
- Decision rules:
  - If weekly SQ average <6 for 3+ sessions → scale back volume and shorten finishers.
  - If key rep totals drop <70% of normal and SQ low → accept temporary dip or add an extra recovery day.
  - If bodyweight trends >+1.5 kg in a week → reduce snacks/added carbs by ~100–200 kcal and increase walking; if –1.5 kg → add 150–300 kcal/day for energy.

Food on travel days (simple, restaurant & room‑service friendly)
- Breakfast: omelette with veg + whole‑grain toast OR Greek yogurt + fruit + granola OR oatmeal with milk and nuts.
- Lunch: grilled chicken/fish/tofu salad or grain bowl; dressing on side.
- Dinner: grilled protein + steamed/roasted veg + small starch (rice/sweet potato).
- Snacks: Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, boiled eggs, tuna packets, protein bar, fruit, nuts, jerky.
- Pre/post workout: small carb + protein (banana + yogurt, toast + nut butter, chicken sandwich).
- Drinks: water, coffee/tea (low sugar), limit alcohol to 1 max and avoid heavy sugary drinks.
- Restaurant tips: ask for grilled, sauce/dressing on side, extra veg, half portions boxed immediately if large.

If she’s nervous about losing muscle: Week 2 is intentionally a bit harder and includes specific overloads (pauses, negatives, isometrics, extra reps/sets) so she should feel progress and maintain confidence.

Additional coaching notes
- Emphasize form and controlled eccentrics — they preserve stimulus when load is limited.
- Keep sessions 30–60 min total including finishers. Focus on quality over quantity.
- Use Active‑Rest Day 4 Week 1 if tired — recovery is a training tool too.
- Encourage tracking SQ + one objective rep total + one weekly weight to avoid overreacting to short‑term noise.
